draft.briefing: Hey, you're in Nagarhole! This forest was declared India's 37th Tiger Reserve in 2003, and it's home to Bengal tigers, Indian elephants, leopards and gaur.
draft.hungryLine: Out here it's simple food, but around Karnataka look out for bisibele baath, a hot rice and lentil dish, and crisp dosas with fresh chutney.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Nagarhole National Park starts about a 5 min walk from here, with forest, small streams, hills, valleys and waterfalls.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a quiet spot by the forest edge and just listen. This park is all streams, hills and valleys.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Karnataka has the largest population of tigers in the world, and Nagarhole is one of its tiger reserves.

spots.name: Nagarhole National Park
spots.detail: 5 min walk · Tigers, elephants, chital and sambar deer

tips.title: Watch for big animals.
tips.body: The park has Bengal tigers, leopards, gaur and Indian elephants, so stay alert and keep your distance.

tips.title: Come after the rains for waterfalls.
tips.body: Across Karnataka, waterfalls are at their best from June to October.

story.title: A wild forest
story.body: Nagarhole spreads across Kodagu and Mysore districts, with rich forest cover, small streams, hills, valleys and waterfalls.

story.title: A tiger reserve
story.body: The park was declared the 37th Tiger Reserve of India in 2003.

story.title: Part of something bigger
story.body: Nagarhole is part of the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve.

story.title: UNESCO hopes
story.body: The Western Ghats Nilgiri Sub-Cluster, including all of Nagarhole, is under consideration by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.
